messages:
elaine: quick follow-up to the RFC — we need to pick a concrete backfill approach for traces that were ingested before the new enrichment pipeline landed in VPC/private customers. TL;DR: private customers often block our KMS access so we can't re-encrypt/decrypt externally. options: (A) sidecar replay on-customer-host (streaming, low latency, needs sidecar deploy), (B) offline within-customer batch rewriter (runs in their infra, higher latency), (C) gated proxy in their VPC with delegated KMS token (operationally heavy). thoughts?

rashid: important constraint: any approach that needs us to touch raw PII is a non-starter for several customers. they only allow a local job that never leaves the VPC. so A or B likely.

kevin: agree. quick cost note: streaming sidecar (A) keeps window small but multiplies traffic while it replays. for a 30d backlog could be 5-10x usual ingest for a week depending on batch parallelism. that spikes cost and could blow SLOs.

anna: +1 to cost spike concern. also we must preserve billing attribution keys for those traces. if we mutate envelope during backfill we need deterministic mapping to original billing key. otherwise chargeback will be wrong.

elaine: actionable checklist I think: 1) we define a minimal transform that only adds enrichment keys (no PII transformations), 2) create an idempotent rewrite mode that writes to new topic with same billing key header, 3) provide a dry-run that emits metrics but doesn't publish. which of the three approaches (A/B/C) supports that most cleanly?

kevin: B (offline batch rewriter) fits 1–3 best. it's easy to run behind customer controls, deterministic, and can do dry-run. downside: backlog TTL and SLO exposure — app teams expect new traces in product views within hours, not days.

rashid: can we do a hybrid: run B (offline) but with a small coordinator in our control plane that pulls progress metadata and drives parallelism based on capacity? coordinator only receives progress markers, no payloads. that lets us throttle to avoid SLO spikes while still offloading the heavy work to customer infra.

anna: hybrid seems pragmatic. need to confirm legal on 'progress markers' — they can't contain any sensitive ids. keep them coarse: shard id + counts + checkpoint timestamp.

elaine: SRE question: how do we avoid double-counting ingestion cost and metrics when the backfill republishes? we need a flag in the envelope that downstreams ignore for billing, but that flag must be verifiable (signed) so customers can't spoof it.

kevin: proposal: backfill envelopes include header X-Backfill-Version and a signature computed with a per-customer HMAC key (customer-provided). verification happens in the ingest gateway; if verified, billing pipeline tags as 'backfill-replay' and excludes from billed delta. this works for VPC where customer manages the HMAC secret.

rashid: edge case: customers that can't run anything (air-gapped). for them we should offer a paid on-site service or a managed appliance image that runs the offline rewriter in their network. documented SLA and runbook.

anna: ops runbook note: must include rollback steps to revert any accidental enrichment — how do we restore original views? keep a pre-backfill snapshot index for 48–72h. cost for snapshoting is small relative to risk.

elaine: ok next steps: - Rashid to validate legal on progress markers (ETA EOD) - Kevin to produce cost delta estimate for sidecar vs batch (by EOW) - Anna to draft runbook skeleton and snapshot retention proposal (tomorrow) - I'll draft a short customer-facing playbook explaining options and tradeoffs.

sre-bot: deployment checklist created: https://internal/redwood/deploy-checks/obs-backfill. contains preflight + dry-run tests + monitoring thresholds.

kevin: one more thing — add an automatic throttling policy in the coordinator that targets 60% of historical peak ingest to avoid unexpected pressure.

elaine: agreed. thanks all — i'll synthesize into RFC follow-up doc and ping infra for budgetary approval. :white_check_mark:
